props.name: attributes
props.description:
You can set every SVG and HTML visualization object to have a custom DOM attributes, which is useful when you want to do unit or end-to-end testing. Attributes configuration object has the following structure:

{
 [selectorString]: {
     [attributeName]: attribute constant value or accessor function
 }
}

e.g.:

{
 [Area.selectors.area]: {
   "test-value": d => d.value
 }
}
props.type: { [selector: string]: { [attr: string]: string | number | boolean | ((datum: any) => string | number | boolean); }; }

props.name: baseline
props.description: Baseline accessor function for stacked values, useful with stacked areas. Default: null

props.name: circleRadius
props.description: Radius of crosshair circles in pixels. Default: 3

props.name: color
props.description: Optional color array or color accessor function for crosshair circles. Default: d => d.color

props.name: contentComponent
props.description: Vue component rendered as the crosshair tooltip content.

props.name: contentProps
props.description: Props passed to contentComponent in addition to payload, config, and x.

props.name: duration
props.description: Animation duration of the data update transitions in milliseconds. Default: 600

props.name: events
props.description:
Events configuration. An object containing properties in the following format:

{
 [selectorString]: {
     [eventType]: callbackFunction
 }
}

e.g.:

{
 [Area.selectors.area]: {
   click: (d) => console.log("Clicked Area", d)
 }
}
props.type: { [selector: string]: { scroll?: VisEventCallback; select?: VisEventCallback; dblclick?: VisEventCallback; touchstart?: VisEventCallback; touchmove?: VisEventCallback; touchend?: VisEventCallback; mouseover?: VisEventCallback; mousemove?: VisEventCallback; mousedown?: VisEventCallback; mouseup?: VisEventCallback; click?: VisEventCallback; auxclick?: VisEventCallback; contextmenu?: VisEventCallback; mouseenter?: VisEventCallback; mouseleave?: VisEventCallback; mouseout?: VisEventCallback; wheel?: VisEventCallback; pointerdown?: VisEventCallback; pointerup?: VisEventCallback; pointerout?: VisEventCallback; pointermove?: VisEventCallback; }; }

props.name: excludeFromDomainCalculation
props.description: Identifies whether the component should be excluded from overall X and Y domain calculations or not. This property can be useful when you want pass individual data to a component and you don't want it to affect the scales of the chart. Default: false

props.name: forceShowAt
props.description: Force the crosshair to show at a specific position. Default: undefined

props.name: getCircles
props.description: Custom function for setting up the crosshair circles, usually needed when snapToData is set to false. The function receives the horizontal position of the crosshair (in the data space, not in pixels), the data array, the yScale instance to help you calculate the correct vertical position of the circles, and the nearest datum index. It has to return an array of the CrosshairCircle objects: { y: number; color: string; opacity?: number }[]. Default: undefined
props.type: ((x: number | Date, data: Datum[], yScale: ContinuousScale, leftNearestDatumIndex?: number) => CrosshairCircle[])

props.name: hideWhenFarFromPointer
props.description: Hide Crosshair when the corresponding datum element is far from mouse pointer. Default: true

props.name: hideWhenFarFromPointerDistance
props.description: Distance in pixels to check in the hideWhenFarFromPointer condition. Default: 100

props.name: id
props.description: Accessor function for getting the unique data record id. Used for more persistent data updates. Default: (d, i) => d.id ?? i

props.name: onCrosshairMove
props.description:
Callback function that is called when the crosshair is moved:

  • x is the horizontal position of the crosshair in the data space;
  • datum is the nearest datum to the crosshair;
  • datumIndex is the index of the nearest datum.
  • event is the event that triggered the crosshair move (mouse or wheel).

When the mouse goes out of the container and on wheel events, all the arguments are undefined except for event. Default: undefined
props.type: ((x?: number | Date, datum?: Datum, datumIndex?: number, event?: MouseEvent | WheelEvent) => void)

props.name: skipRangeCheck
props.description: Skip range checks for crosshair visibility. When true, crosshair will show regardless of position within chart bounds. Default: false This is useful for testing, especially when you only triggers mousemove event but does not have real mouse event.

props.name: snapToData
props.description: Snap to the nearest data point. If disabled, the tooltip template will receive only the horizontal position of the crosshair and you'll be responsible for getting the underlying data records and crosshair circles (see the getCircles configuration option). Default: true

props.name: strokeColor
props.description: Optional stroke color accessor function for crosshair circles. Default: undefined

props.name: strokeWidth
props.description: Optional stroke width for crosshair circles. Default: undefined

props.name: tooltip
props.description: An instance of the Tooltip component to be used with Crosshair. Default: undefined

props.name: visibilityThreshold
props.description: Minimum fraction (0 to 1) of the container's area that must be visible in the viewport for the Crosshair (and its Tooltip) to be displayed. This prevents the Crosshair from showing when the chart is mostly scrolled out of view. Charts that are wider or taller than the viewport may never reach the default ratio, so lower this value (or set it to 0 to always show the Crosshair) for large charts. Default: 0.35

props.name: x
props.description: Optional accessor function for getting the values along the X axis. Default: undefined

props.name: xScale
props.description: Scale for X dimension, e.g. Scale.scaleLinear(). If you set xScale you'll be responsible for setting it's domain and range as well. Only continuous scales are supported. Default: undefined

props.name: y
props.description: Optional single of multiple accessor functions for getting the values along the Y axis. Default: undefined

props.name: yScale
props.description: Scale for Y dimension, e.g. Scale.scaleLinear(). If you set yScale you'll be responsible for setting it's domain and range as well. Only continuous scales are supported. Default: undefined

props.name: yStacked
props.description: Separate array of accessors for stacked components (eg StackedBar, Area). Default: undefined
